Thanks again for the demo earlier. We reviewed the sample usage export (attached) and have two billing questions before we lock the pilot SOW:

1) Partial-token rounding: our ingestion has many short requests (~6–40 tokens). Do you round per-call, per-session, or aggregate across a conversation window? Example: if we send 3 calls of 7 tokens each, how does that bill?

2) Context stitching (KV / prefix cache): we plan to stitch a 1.5k token knowledge prefix onto many short calls. Is that charged every call or do you apply a cached prefix credit when repeated across calls? Also curious about how streaming responses impact rounding (partial streaming chunks).

Could you provide 2–3 concrete examples with numbers we can model into our forecast? I've attached our sample export (SaaSHealth_usage_sample.csv) and a sketch of expected call patterns.

Thanks Sarah — great questions. High level answers up front: we charge on a per-token basis but apply an aggregation window and a configurable rounding quantum to reduce high-cardinality micro-charges. Cache credits apply when the same prefix is served from the KV cache without recomputing tokens.

I'm attaching a pilot pricing sheet that includes three worked examples based on the sample export you sent. Quick bullets:
- Default aggregation window: 5 minutes per conversation by default (can be reduced to per-call for low-latency apps)
- Rounding quantum: 16-token buckets by default for hosted plans; enterprise pilots can negotiate 8-token buckets or opt for per-token granularity.
- KV cache: repeated prefix that hits the cache is billed as "cached prefix delta" (small delta tokens) not the full prefix on every call.

Next steps: I'll have Karthik add numeric examples (he's included below) and Evelyn will confirm whether we can waive minimums for the 30-day pilot. If those look good we'll update the SOW and route to DocuSign.

Hi all — following up with concrete arithmetic so Sarah can plug numbers into the forecast. Below are three representative scenarios using Redwood hosted defaults (5m aggregation window, 16-token quantum).

Scenario A — three short calls, no cache:
- Call 1: request 7 tokens, response 12 tokens => total 19 tokens => rounded up to 32 (one 16-token quantum rounds to 32 in our bucket policy for small totals)
- Call 2: request 6 tokens, response 9 tokens => total 15 => rounded up to 16
- Call 3: request 9 tokens, response 11 tokens => total 20 => rounded up to 32
- Aggregation: if these three calls occur inside the 5-minute conversation window, we aggregate tokens first: 19+15+20=54 => rounding => 64 (4 quanta). So aggregation reduces bill from 80 -> 64 tokens equivalent.

Scenario B — repeated prefix (1,500 tokens) + short delta, prefix hits KV cache on calls 2..N:
- First call (cache miss): prefix 1,500 + delta 30 => billed tokens 1,530 => rounding/quantum -> bill as 1536 (rounding up to nearest 16)
- Subsequent calls (cache hit): cached prefix credited; only delta 30 + cache-serve delta (we count small KV read tokens, typically 2–6 tokens worth) => 36 tokens => rounded to 48 per call. So effective amortized cost after ~10 calls is heavily reduced.

Scenario C — streaming response, partial chunking:
- We measure tokens at record boundaries; streaming doesn't change token accounting, but partial-chunk emissions may produce additional micro-billing if your client acknowledges partial payloads as separate calls. For long streaming outputs we recommend batching acknowledgements to avoid extra round-trips.

Notes / negotiable items:
- For pilots we can set quantum to 8 tokens for the first 30 days so your short-call-heavy pattern bills closer to raw tokens.
- If you prefer pure per-token billing we can offer that as a bespoke option with minimum monthly commit.

I've uploaded a short set of worked examples here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-token-examples and attached token_examples.md with the arithmetic.

Hi Sarah — quick finance confirmation:
- TTL / eviction: cache TTL is policy-driven; default is 24h for prefix caches in hosted mode (can be configured). Eviction occurs on a least-recently-used basis; if you refresh every 24h you will generally see cache hits for the day.
- 8-token quantum concession: we can apply the 8-token quantum for the pilot period and offer to retroactively reprice any usage from the pilot start date up to signature provided you send a signed SOW within 14 days.
- Minimums: we will waive the monthly minimum for the first 30 days of the pilot. After that normal minimums apply unless you commit to an annual reserved capacity.

I'll prepare a short addendum to the SOW and send a DocuSign link.
